intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years. Then walk to the stunning Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) with its six minarets and exquisite Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context on Byzantine and Ottoman history.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and local spices. Engage with vendors, taste free samples, and soak in centuries of trading culture. Ideal for picking up authentic local ingredients and souvenirs.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Visit the Imperial Treasury, sacred relics, and the legendary Harem quarters. The palace offers breathtaking views of the Bosphorus and houses priceless artifacts including the Topkapi Dagger and the Spoonmaker's Diamond.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Breakfast & Bosphorus Ferry Cruise
experiences.description: Start with an authentic Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) featuring olives, white cheese, tomatoes, cucumbers, honey, clotted cream, and simit at a local tea garden. Then board a public Bosphorus ferry for a scenic cruise between Europe and Asia, passing Ottoman palaces, wooden yalı mansions, and historic fortresses. A deeply local and affordable cultural experience.

experiences.name: Balık Ekmek, Meyhane Dinner & Kadıköy Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Cross to the Asian side for an immersive street food tour of Kadıköy market, sampling balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich), kokoreç, fresh mussels, and börek. In the evening, dine at a traditional meyhane (Turkish tavern) in Beyoğlu with meze platters, raki, and live fasıl music — a true taste of Istanbul's vibrant local food and nightlife culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Havaist airport bus or Metro M11 line to the city center (budget option ~₺50-70). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Grab a late-night snack near the hotel and get rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near hotel: simit (sesame bread ring) or a döner wrap from a 24-hour street stall (~₺50-80)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Turkish Lira handy for transport from the airport. The Havaist bus is the cheapest airport transfer option. Avoid taxi touts inside the terminal — use official metered taxis or public transport.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start after late arrival. Enjoy a traditional Turkish breakfast at a local kahvaltı (breakfast) café near the hotel — olives, cheese, eggs, tomatoes, and çay (tea). Then take a leisurely walk along the beachfront promenade to get oriented with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a public ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı ferry terminal (depending on hotel location). Visit Büyükada, the largest island. Rent a bicycle (~₺150/hr) or take a horse-drawn carriage to explore the island's car-free streets, pine forests, and historic Greek Orthodox monastery (Aya Yorgi Church). Stunning Bosphorus views included.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to the mainland by sunset. Stroll along the waterfront and enjoy the golden hour views. Have dinner at a local balık ekmek (fish sandwich) stand near the ferry docks.

meals.breakfast: Local kahvaltı café near hotel — full Turkish breakfast spread (~₺80-120 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic or grab gözleme (stuffed flatbread) and ayran (yogurt drink) from a street vendor on Büyükada (~₺60-90)
meals.dinner: Balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) at a waterfront stall near the ferry terminal (~₺50-70)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets to Princes' Islands cost approximately ₺30-50 each way using an İstanbulkart (rechargeable transit card). Buy an İstanbulkart on Day 2 — it saves money on all public transport throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to the Old City (Sultanahmet). Visit the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — now a mosque and free to enter. Arrive early (opens at 9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. Marvel at the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and centuries of layered history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 5 minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — free entry. Admire the stunning Iznik tile interior and six minarets. Then explore the Hippodrome Square (Sultanahmet Meydanı) with the Obelisk of Theodosius and Serpent Column — all free. Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) nearby (~₺250 entry) — an atmospheric underground Byzantine water cistern.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Sultanahmet neighborhood at dusk. Enjoy the illuminated mosques and atmospheric streets. Have dinner at a local lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) in the area.

meals.breakfast: Simit and çay from a street cart in Sultanahmet (~₺30-40)
meals.lunch: Pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a budget pide salonu near Sultanahmet (~₺80-120)
meals.dinner: Lokanta-style meal — lentil soup, rice, and a meat or vegetable stew at a neighborhood canteen (~₺100-150)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for mosque visits — shoulders and knees covered. Women should carry a headscarf. Remove shoes before entering mosques. The İstanbulkart covers tram T1 line which runs directly to Sultanahmet.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapı Palace (Topkapı Sarayı) — the magnificent Ottoman imperial palace overlooking the Bosphorus and Golden Horn. Entry ~₺500. Explore the Imperial Treasury, Harem (extra ticket ~₺200), and the sacred relics pavilion. Arrive at 9:00 AM opening to beat tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Gülhane Park (free) — a beautiful rose garden adjacent to Topkapı, perfect for a relaxing stroll. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (İstanbul Arkeoloji Müzeleri) next door (~₺200) — home to the stunning Alexander Sarcophagus and ancient artifacts from across the Ottoman Empire.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down to the Eminönü waterfront. Watch the fishermen on Galata Bridge and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Cross the bridge on foot for great Golden Horn views.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at a café near Sultanahmet (~₺80-100)
meals.lunch: Köfte ekmek (meatball sandwich) from a street vendor near Eminönü (~₺50-70)
meals.dinner: Soup and bread at a çorba evi (soup house) near Eminönü — mercimek çorbası (red lentil soup) is a staple (~₺60-90)

day_by_day.notes: Topkapı Palace is closed on Tuesdays — plan accordingly. Museum Pass Istanbul (~₺1,200) covers Topkapı, Archaeological Museums, and several other major museums and pays for itself in 2-3 visits.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with 4,000+ shops. Open 9:00 AM–7:00 PM, closed Sundays. Browse spices, textiles, ceramics, and jewelry. Practice your bargaining skills — prices are always negotiable. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı / Egyptian Bazaar) nearby — a smaller but equally vibrant market specializing in spices, dried fruits, Turkish delight, and teas. Great place to buy affordable food souvenirs. Then explore the surrounding Eminönü neighborhood and its street food scene.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short ferry ride across the Golden Horn to Karaköy neighborhood. Walk up to the Galata Tower area (~₺350 entry to climb the tower for panoramic city views, or admire it from outside for free). Explore the bohemian streets around Galata.

meals.breakfast: Börek (flaky pastry with cheese or spinach) from a neighborhood bakery (~₺40-60)
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Eminönü: midye dolma (stuffed mussels, sold per piece ~₺5-8 each) and fresh pomegranate juice (~₺30)
meals.dinner: Meyhane-style dinner in Karaköy — meze plates and bread at a budget taverna (~₺150-200)

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Don't feel pressured to buy — browsing is perfectly acceptable. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Süleymaniye Mosque (Süleymaniye Camii) — the grandest Ottoman imperial mosque in Istanbul, built by Sinan for Suleiman the Magnificent. Free entry. Stunning architecture and hilltop views over the Golden Horn. Explore the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) including tombs of Suleiman and his wife Hürrem Sultan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fatih neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most traditional and conservative districts. Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) — Byzantine mosaics and frescoes of extraordinary quality (~₺200 entry). Walk through the old Byzantine land walls (Theodosian Walls) — a UNESCO World Heritage site you can explore for free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Beyoğlu district. Walk the famous İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's bustling pedestrian boulevard lined with shops, cafés, and historic buildings. Ride the nostalgic red tram that runs along the avenue (costs one İstanbulkart fare).

meals.breakfast: Menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local kahvaltı spot (~₺80-100)
meals.lunch: Kuru fasulye (white bean stew) with rice and bread at a traditional lokanta in Fatih (~₺80-100) — a classic budget Istanbul meal
meals.dinner: Street food on İstiklal: kokoreç (seasoned offal sandwich) or a dürüm wrap (~₺70-100)

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may have restricted access if restoration work is ongoing — check ahead. Fatih is a conservative neighborhood; dress modestly out of respect.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü or Beşiktaş — the regular commuter ferry (not the tourist cruise) travels up the Bosphorus for a fraction of the price (~₺30-50 with İstanbulkart). Enjoy views of Ottoman palaces, yalıs (wooden waterfront mansions), and the two Bosphorus bridges. Ride to Anadolu Kavağı at the mouth of the Black Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Anadolu Kavağı village — climb up to the Genoese Castle (Yoros Kalesi) ruins for sweeping views of where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Completely free and rewarding. Browse the small fishing village below.
day_by_day.evening: Take the return ferry back to the European side as the sun sets over the Bosphorus — one of Istanbul's most beautiful and free experiences. Arrive back in the city by early evening.

meals.breakfast: Simit and çay at the ferry terminal (~₺30-40)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at one of the simple seafood restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı — ask for the daily catch and negotiate a fair price (~₺150-200 for a full meal)
meals.dinner: Döner kebab or lahmacun (Turkish flatbread with minced meat) near the hotel (~₺80-120)

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry (Şehir Hatları) is dramatically cheaper than tourist Bosphorus cruises and offers the same views. Check the ferry schedule in advance as return ferries from Anadolu Kavağı are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) in Beşiktaş — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore where Atatürk died in 1938. Entry ~₺500, guided tours only. Arrive at opening (9:00 AM) to secure a spot on the first tour. The crystal staircase and 4.5-ton chandelier are highlights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to Beşiktaş market area — a lively neighborhood with a great street market. Explore the waterfront and the Çırağan Palace exterior (now a luxury hotel, but the gardens and exterior are photogenic). Visit Yıldız Park (free) — a beautiful forested Ottoman park with pavilions.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Ortaköy neighborhood — a charming village-like district beneath the Bosphorus Bridge. Famous for its kumpir (loaded baked potatoes — a must-try Istanbul street food) and waffles. The Ortaköy Mosque lit up at night with the bridge in the background is iconic.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at a café in Beşiktaş (~₺90-120)
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş market food — grilled corn, fresh fruit, and a sandwich (~₺60-80)
meals.dinner: Kumpir in Ortaköy — a large baked potato loaded with butter, cheese, and toppings of your choice (~₺80-120). A legendary Istanbul street food experience.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. The palace tour is mandatory and lasts about 1.5 hours. Ortaköy is very lively on weekends with an outdoor craft market.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Kadıköy neighborhood on the Asian side of Istanbul — take a short ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy (~₺30 with İstanbulkart). Kadıköy is Istanbul's hippest, most vibrant district. Visit the Kadıköy Bazaar (Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a covered market full of fresh produce, spices, cheeses, olives, and street food. A feast for the senses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Moda neighborhood — a charming residential area of Kadıköy with tree-lined streets, independent cafés, and beautiful Bosphorus views. Walk along the Moda coastline promenade. Visit Haydarpaşa Train Station — a stunning neo-Gothic German-built railway terminal on the Bosphorus shore (exterior viewing, currently under renovation).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the evening in Kadıköy's bar and restaurant street (Kadife Sokak, known as 'Bar Street'). Lively atmosphere with live music spilling out of venues. Take the ferry back to the European side.

meals.breakfast: Islak hamburger (steamed burger) or a classic Turkish breakfast in Kadıköy market (~₺60-90)
meals.lunch: Graze through Kadıköy Bazaar — buy fresh produce, cheese, olives, and bread for a self-assembled picnic lunch (~₺80-100)
meals.dinner: Çiğ köfte (spiced bulgur rolls) and ayran on Kadife Sokak, or a budget meyhane with meze (~₺120-160)

day_by_day.notes: Kadıköy is considered by many locals to be the best neighborhood in Istanbul for food. The ferry ride itself offers great views of the Istanbul skyline and is one of the best budget activities in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) in Karaköy (~₺200 entry) — Turkey's leading contemporary art museum with rotating exhibitions and permanent collection showcasing Turkish modern art. Stunning location right on the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Karaköy and Tophane neighborhoods — trendy areas with art galleries, design shops, and historic Ottoman buildings. Visit the Kılıç Ali Paşa Mosque (free) — a beautiful 16th-century mosque by Sinan. Walk up through Galata and into Beyoğlu. Explore the Pera Museum (~₺200) — houses Orientalist paintings and the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event — check local listings for free concerts, gallery openings, or cultural events at the Atatürk Cultural Center (AKM) or neighborhood spaces. Alternatively, enjoy a çay (tea) session at a traditional çay bahçesi (tea garden) in Beyoğlu.

meals.breakfast: Açma (soft bread roll) and çay from a Karaköy bakery (~₺30-50)
meals.lunch: Balık ekmek or a quick pide at a budget spot in Karaköy (~₺70-100)
meals.dinner: Manti (Turkish dumplings with yogurt and butter sauce) at a neighborhood restaurant in Beyoğlu (~₺120-160)

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern may have free admission days — check their website. The Karaköy area has excellent specialty coffee shops if you need a caffeine fix. Many galleries in Beyoğlu have free entry.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Eyüp Sultan Mosque and neighborhood — one of the holiest sites in Istanbul, located at the end of the Golden Horn. Take a ferry up the Golden Horn (Haliç ferry line) or bus. The mosque complex is free and spiritually significant. Climb to the Pierre Loti Café by cable car (₺30) or on foot for panoramic Golden Horn views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk back along the Golden Horn waterfront through Balat and Fener neighborhoods — two of Istanbul's oldest and most atmospheric districts. Balat has a colorful, photogenic streetscape with Jewish, Greek, and Armenian heritage. Explore the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate (Ekümenik Patrikane) — free to visit. Browse Balat's antique shops and vintage stores.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European city center. Visit a traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse) for an authentic cultural experience — try Cemberlitas Hamami or Çukurcuma Hamami. Budget options start from ~₺300-400 for a basic bath and scrub.

meals.breakfast: Traditional breakfast at a Eyüp café (~₺80-100)
meals.lunch: Balat street food — Armenian or Jewish-influenced pastries and snacks from local bakeries (~₺60-80)
meals.dinner: Beyoğlu neighborhood restaurant — mercimek köftesi (lentil patties) and salad, a popular vegetarian budget meal (~₺90-120)

day_by_day.notes: Balat is extremely photogenic — bring your camera. The neighborhood has been gentrifying but retains its authentic character. Dress modestly in Eyüp as it is a very religious neighborhood.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bursa — take an early morning ferry from Yenikapı to Bursa (Mudanya) or a direct fast ferry (~₺150-200 one way). Bursa was the first Ottoman capital and is a UNESCO World Heritage city. Visit the Grand Mosque (Ulu Cami) — free, with stunning calligraphy. Explore the Bursa Covered Bazaar (Kapalı Çarşı).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Green Mosque (Yeşil Cami) and Green Tomb (Yeşil Türbe) — masterpieces of early Ottoman architecture with extraordinary Iznik tile work. Free entry to the mosque; small fee for the tomb. Take a cable car up Uludağ mountain for views (optional, ~₺100 return). Explore the Cumalıkızık village — a perfectly preserved Ottoman village on the outskirts of Bursa.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by ferry in the evening. Bursa is famous for İskender kebab — treat yourself to this dish before departing.

meals.breakfast: Quick simit and çay at the ferry terminal before departure (~₺30-40)
meals.lunch: Authentic İskender kebab in Bursa — the dish was invented here. Budget restaurants serve it for ~₺150-200
meals.dinner: Light dinner back in Istanbul near the hotel after the return journey (~₺80-120)

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion — start early (7:00-8:00 AM) to maximize time in Bursa. Check ferry schedules in advance and book return tickets. Bursa is about 2.5-3 hours from Istanbul including the ferry crossing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — revisit your favorite neighborhood or spot you didn't have time for. Consider a morning walk along the Bosphorus waterfront near the hotel to soak in the views one last time. Pick up last-minute souvenirs from the Spice Bazaar or local shops — Turkish tea, spices, Turkish delight, and evil eye (nazar) amulets are great affordable gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit any remaining must-see sites. The Miniaturk open-air museum in Eyüp (~₺150) has 1/25 scale models of Turkey's greatest monuments — a fun and affordable way to see everything you may have missed. Or simply relax at a waterfront çay bahçesi with a final glass of çay and reflect on the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Pack up, check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, and head to the airport. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights. Use the Metro M11 or Havaist bus for budget airport transfer.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast one final time — a proper send-off at a neighborhood kahvaltı café (~₺100-130)
meals.lunch: Final street food feast — assemble a spread of simit, börek, midye dolma, and fresh juice (~₺80-100)
meals.dinner: Airport food or a quick meal before departure — or pack some Turkish snacks from the bazaar for the flight

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Turkish Lira for airport transport. Exchange or spend remaining lira before departure as Turkish Lira is difficult to exchange abroad. The İstanbulkart can be returned at the airport for a partial refund of the card deposit.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Istanbul on flight UA at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the hotel amenities. Keep the night light and relaxing.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the hotel or a nearby 24-hour lokanta (Turkish diner) — try a simple bowl of mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and bread to ease into local cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Do not over-plan Day 1. Get rest to beat jet lag. Confirm hotel transfer in advance and exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start — enjoy the hotel breakfast and take a morning stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Breathe in the Bosphorus or Sea of Marmara air and orient yourself with the neighborhood. Visit a nearby local simit cart for an authentic Istanbul morning snack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi or tram ride to the Sultanahmet district. Visit the iconic Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) — admire the stunning tilework and six minarets. Walk across the Hippodrome of Constantinople (Sultanahmet Square) to see the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric streets of Sultanahmet at dusk. Enjoy the illuminated view of the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia from the square. Head to a rooftop restaurant in Sultanahmet for dinner with panoramic views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Casual kebab lunch at a neighborhood lokanta near the beachfront — try Adana kebab with rice and salad (budget-friendly, ~150-200 TL)
meals.dinner: Sultanahmet Köftecisi or a mid-range Ottoman cuisine restaurant in Sultanahmet — try köfte (meatballs), pide bread, and ayran (~300-400 TL per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Mosque is free to enter but closed to tourists during prayer times (5 times daily, each closure lasts about 90 minutes). Dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees, and women should bring a headscarf.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — one of the world's greatest architectural achievements, originally a Byzantine cathedral, then an Ottoman mosque, now a functioning mosque and museum. Arrive early (opens at 9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. Marvel at the massive dome, golden mosaics, and layered history spanning 1,500 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Topkapi Palace — the grand seat of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem quarters, and the stunning views of the Bosphorus from the palace terraces. Allow 3-4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Grand Bazaar area (closes around 7 PM) for a quick browse of spices, textiles, and souvenirs. Have dinner in the Eminönü district by the Galata Bridge — watch fishermen and enjoy the lively waterfront atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Simit, börek, and tea from street vendors near Topkapi Palace (~50-80 TL) — an authentic and economical local lunch
meals.dinner: Balık-ekmek (fish sandwich) from the famous boats at Eminönü waterfront, paired with pickled vegetables and ayran (~80-120 TL) — a beloved Istanbul street food experience

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace entrance fee is approximately 500-700 TL; the Harem requires a separate ticket. Hagia Sophia is free but requires modest dress. Book Topkapi tickets online in advance to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — an extraordinary underground Byzantine water reservoir with dramatic lighting, ancient columns, and the famous Medusa head bases. Then walk to the Istanbul Archaeology Museums complex nearby — three museums housing artifacts spanning 5,000 years of civilization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot to the Beyoğlu district. Climb the Galata Tower for panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul, the Bosphorus, and the Golden Horn. Explore the charming streets of Galata and Karaköy — browse independent boutiques, art galleries, and coffee shops.
day_by_day.evening: Walk up Istiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard buzzing with locals, musicians, and shops. Explore the side streets (Çiçek Pasajı, Nevizade Sokak) for meyhane (tavern) culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Karaköy Güllüoğlu — the legendary baklava shop in Karaköy, paired with Turkish tea. Have a light lunch of börek or gözleme at a nearby café (~100-150 TL)
meals.dinner: Meyhane dinner on Nevizade Sokak in Beyoğlu — order a spread of cold and hot meze (hummus, dolma, cacık, arnavut ciğeri), fresh fish, and rakı (~400-600 TL per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern recently underwent renovation — confirm opening hours in advance. Galata Tower has an entrance fee (~200-300 TL). Istiklal Avenue is best experienced in the early evening when it comes alive with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü — one of Istanbul's oldest and most aromatic covered markets. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, spices, and herbal teas. Shop for authentic local products to take home. Explore the surrounding streets for a raw local market experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a public ferry (vapur) from Eminönü across to the Asian side of Istanbul — the Kadıköy district. This short Bosphorus crossing (~25-30 minutes) is a highlight in itself. Explore Kadıköy's vibrant food market (Kadıköy Çarşısı), street art, and bohemian café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Wander Kadıköy's Moda neighborhood along the waterfront promenade at sunset. Take the evening ferry back to the European side, watching Istanbul's skyline glow at dusk — one of the most beautiful sights in the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Kadıköy market food tour — graze on kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), fresh fruit, and börek from market stalls (~150-200 TL total)
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — a legendary restaurant serving rare Anatolian regional dishes and traditional recipes from across Turkey (~300-400 TL per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy costs only a few lira with an Istanbulkart (transit card). Purchase an Istanbulkart if you haven't already — it saves money on all public transport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace on the European Bosphorus shore — the ornate 19th-century Ottoman palace that replaced Topkapi as the imperial residence. Tour the stunning ceremonial halls, crystal staircase, and the room where Atatürk passed away in 1938. The palace blends Ottoman and European Baroque styles magnificently.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a taxi to Beşiktaş neighborhood — a lively, authentic Istanbul district. Explore the Beşiktaş fish market, browse local shops, and visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) showcasing Ottoman maritime history and imperial caiques (royal rowboats).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood for evening window shopping along its elegant boulevards. Enjoy the contrast between this modern, fashionable district and the historic areas visited earlier in the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş fish market area — fresh grilled fish sandwich or a sit-down fish restaurant with Bosphorus views (~250-350 TL)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Nişantaşı — try modern Turkish cuisine with creative takes on classic dishes (~400-500 TL per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires a guided tour (mandatory) — book tickets in advance online (~500-700 TL). Tours run at set times. Photography is restricted inside. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Bosphorus cruise — take a public ferry (the long Bosphorus tour from Eminönü) that travels up the Bosphorus strait past palaces, fortresses, wooden yalı mansions, and under the iconic Bosphorus Bridge. The journey goes all the way to Anadolu Kavağı at the Black Sea entrance.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Anadolu Kavağı, hike up to the medieval Genoese castle (Yoros Kalesi) for sweeping views of the Bosphorus meeting the Black Sea. Browse the small village's seafood restaurants along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry back to Eminönü (the round trip takes most of the day). Enjoy the golden hour light on the Bosphorus during the return journey. Rest at the hotel or take a quiet evening walk along your beachfront neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — pack snacks for the ferry
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at one of the waterfront restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı — try sea bass (levrek) or sea bream (çipura) with salad and bread (~300-400 TL)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a neighborhood restaurant near the hotel — try a simple Turkish pide (flatbread pizza) with various toppings (~200-250 TL)

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry (Boğaz Hattı) departs Eminönü at set times (typically 10:35 AM). Purchase tickets at the pier. The full round trip takes approximately 6-7 hours. This is one of Istanbul's best-value experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably the most magnificent Ottoman mosque in Istanbul, designed by the legendary architect Sinan in the 16th century. Explore the mosque complex including the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan. Enjoy views over the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Fatih and Zeyrek neighborhoods — among Istanbul's oldest and most authentic. Visit the Zeyrek Mosque (formerly the Byzantine Church of the Pantocrator), walk through traditional Ottoman wooden house streets, and experience a neighborhood far off the typical tourist trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet for the Sound and Light Show at the Blue Mosque (seasonal, evening performances). Alternatively, take a night walk along the old city walls near Topkapi and enjoy the illuminated skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the traditional lokanta restaurants in the Süleymaniye area — these worker's restaurants serve home-style Turkish food at very affordable prices (~150-200 TL for a full meal)
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi or a similar historic restaurant in Sultanahmet — classic Turkish comfort food in a historic setting (~250-350 TL)

day_by_day.notes: The Fatih and Zeyrek neighborhoods are best explored on foot. Wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobblestoned and hilly. This area gives an authentic glimpse into everyday Istanbul life away from tourist crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse) — book a session at one of Istanbul's historic hammams such as Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584) or Cağaloğlu Hamamı. Enjoy the full ritual: steam room, kese (exfoliating scrub), and foam massage. A deeply cultural and rejuvenating experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) on the Bosphorus waterfront in Karaköy — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum showcasing modern Turkish and international art. The building itself is architecturally striking with beautiful water views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tophane and Cihangir neighborhoods — artsy, bohemian areas beloved by Istanbul's creative community. Browse independent galleries, vintage shops, and cozy cafés. Cihangir has some of Istanbul's best café culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Cihangir café lunch — try menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) or a gözleme (stuffed flatbread) at a local café (~150-200 TL)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Cihangir — a neighborhood restaurant serving modern Turkish cuisine in a relaxed, local atmosphere (~350-450 TL per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book hammam sessions in advance, especially on weekends. Prices range from 500-1,500 TL depending on the package. The full experience (steam + scrub + massage) is highly recommended. Istanbul Modern has an entrance fee (~200-300 TL).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands in the Sea of Marmara. These car-free islands are a peaceful escape from the city, with Victorian-era mansions, pine forests, and horse-drawn carriages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Büyükada by horse-drawn phaeton (fayton) or bicycle — tour the island's charming streets, visit the hilltop Aya Yorgi (St. George) Monastery for panoramic sea views, and relax on the waterfront promenade. The island has a distinctly different pace from mainland Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: Take the evening ferry back to Istanbul, watching the city's skyline emerge across the water as you approach. Arrive back refreshed and with a new perspective on Istanbul's geography.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a simit and tea at the ferry terminal
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at one of Büyükada's waterfront fish restaurants — try fried calamari, grilled fish, and meze with a sea view (~350-500 TL)
meals.dinner: Dinner near the hotel — try a neighborhood pide restaurant or a casual Turkish restaurant for a relaxed evening (~200-300 TL)

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Büyükada depart regularly from Kabataş (IDO or Şehir Hatları ferries). The journey takes 60-90 minutes. Bicycles can be rented on the island (~100-150 TL/hour). The island gets crowded on weekends — a weekday visit is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Chora Church (Kariye Camii/Museum) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to the most spectacular Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, even surpassing those in Hagia Sophia. The 14th-century artwork depicting the life of Christ and the Virgin Mary is breathtaking. Explore the surrounding ancient city walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along a section of the ancient Theodosian Walls — the massive 5th-century Byzantine fortifications that protected Constantinople for over 1,000 years. Visit the Yedikule Fortress (Castle of the Seven Towers) built into the city walls. This area is deeply atmospheric and largely undiscovered by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Balat and Fener neighborhoods along the Golden Horn — Istanbul's most colorful and historically layered districts, home to ancient Greek Orthodox, Jewish, and Armenian communities. Walk the rainbow-painted streets of Balat at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Local lunch in the Balat neighborhood — try one of the charming small restaurants or cafés in the colorful streets (~200-250 TL)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fener/Balat — several excellent restaurants have opened in this gentrifying area, serving both traditional and contemporary Turkish food (~300-400 TL)

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may have restricted access if ongoing restoration work is underway — confirm before visiting. The Balat neighborhood is best explored on foot; the streets are narrow and steep. This area offers some of Istanbul's best photography opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) properly — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops across 61 covered streets. Spend the morning exploring its labyrinthine passages, practicing the art of bargaining, and shopping for quality Turkish goods: ceramics, carpets, jewelry, leather, and textiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cooking class or food tour in Istanbul — join a guided walking food tour of the Eminönü, Kapalıçarşı, and Tahtakale areas to discover hidden food vendors, taste rare regional Turkish dishes, and learn about the city's culinary geography. Alternatively, visit the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu — a fine art museum with Ottoman-era paintings.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Beyoğlu entertainment district — enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar with Bosphorus views, then explore the lively Asmalımescit neighborhood for your farewell dinner in a meyhane setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Food tour grazing — taste Turkish delight, roasted chestnuts, fresh pomegranate juice, kokoreç, and pastırma (cured beef) throughout the afternoon (~included in tour or ~200-300 TL independently)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Beyoğlu with panoramic Istanbul views — splurge slightly on this final evening (~500-700 TL per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Bargaining is expected and part of the culture — start at 50-60% of the asking price. Keep a copy of your passport or ID when shopping for carpets or expensive items as some shops require it for export documentation.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely last Turkish breakfast at the hotel or at a traditional Turkish breakfast restaurant (kahvaltı salonu). A full Turkish breakfast spread is one of the great culinary experiences: cheeses, olives, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), fresh tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs, and tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute sightseeing based on anything missed — consider a final walk along the Bosphorus waterfront, a visit to a local tea garden (çay bahçesi), or last-minute shopping for souvenirs. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Istanbul Airport (IST) or Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW) for departure. Allow at least 3 hours before flight time for international departures. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional Turkish breakfast spread at Van Kahvaltı Evi or similar kahvaltı restaurant (~200-300 TL per person) — a perfect final Istanbul meal
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or airport area — a simple soup and sandwich or pide (~150-200 TL)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul traffic can be very heavy, especially during rush hours (7-10 AM and 5-8 PM). Allow extra time for airport transfer. The new Istanbul Airport (IST) is approximately 45-60 minutes from the city center in normal traffic, but can take 90+ minutes during peak hours. Consider booking a private transfer in advance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check-in, unwind with a welcome amenity from the resort, and settle into your suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — charcuterie board, Turkish mezze selection, and herbal tea to ease into Istanbul time

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm early check-in or suite readiness with the resort. Keep the first night light — big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a private guided orientation walk through the nearby coastal neighborhood. Absorb the sea air, local market stalls, and the rhythm of Istanbul's waterfront life before diving into the city's historic core.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeured transfer to Sultanahmet — the historic heart of Istanbul. Begin with an exclusive guided tour of the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya), including a detailed exploration of its Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman additions, and architectural grandeur. Follow with a visit to the adjacent Topkapi Palace grounds and its first courtyard.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Sultanahmet Square at golden hour, taking in views of the Blue Mosque illuminated against the evening sky. Return to the resort for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Turkish breakfast spread at Aegean Bliss Resort — simit, white cheese, olives, honey, clotted cream, fresh tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs prepared to order, and Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Matbah Restaurant, Sultanahmet — an Ottoman-inspired fine dining experience within a historic caravanserai setting, serving recipes sourced from 15th-century palace kitchens
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant at Four Seasons Hotel Sultanahmet — elegant Mediterranean-Turkish cuisine with impeccable service and a refined wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book Hagia Sophia timed entry in advance. Hagia Sophia now operates as a mosque — dress modestly and bring a scarf. Private guide strongly recommended for historical depth.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Topkapi Palace — explore the Imperial Harem, the Treasury (housing the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), and the sacred relics in the Pavilion of the Holy Mantle. A dedicated guide will bring the Ottoman sultans' world vividly to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex adjacent to Topkapi — three world-class museums in one compound featuring the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Anatolian artifacts, and the Museum of the Ancient Orient. Then walk down to the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) for an atmospheric underground exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Cross to the Galata district via private transfer. Ascend the Galata Tower for panoramic sunset views over the Bosphorus and the Golden Horn. Dinner in the vibrant Karaköy neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Konyalı Topkapi Restaurant inside the Topkapi Palace grounds — a historic institution serving traditional Turkish cuisine with Bosphorus views
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant, Beyoğlu — Chef Mehmet Gürs's celebrated New Anatolian cuisine on the rooftop of the Marmara Pera hotel, with sweeping city views

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays — confirm the day of visit. Harem requires a separate ticket. Book Mikla well in advance as it is one of Istanbul's most coveted reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Private Bosphorus yacht cruise departing from a nearby marina. Sail past the Dolmabahçe Palace waterfront, the Çırağan Palace, the Rumeli and Anadolu fortresses, and the iconic Bosphorus bridges. Enjoy champagne and fresh fruit on deck as Europe and Asia flank you on either side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dock near Bebek or Arnavutköy — two of Istanbul's most charming Bosphorus villages. Explore boutique shops, art galleries, and the picturesque waterfront promenade. Visit a local pastry shop for a taste of profiteroles or künefe.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Istanbul's premier Bosphorus-view restaurants in the Kuruçeşme or Bebek area, followed by a private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic-style lunch served on board the private yacht — smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, Turkish mezes, fresh bread, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Lacivert Restaurant, Anadoluhisarı — a legendary Bosphorus-side restaurant known for its fresh seafood, mezes, and stunning strait views from the Asian shore

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter at least one week in advance. Confirm weather forecast the day before. Bring light layers as the Bosphorus breeze can be cool in May.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private tour of the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets. With a knowledgeable guide, navigate beyond the tourist facade into the specialized hans (merchant quarters) for carpets, antique jewelry, ceramics, and handcrafted copper. Learn to distinguish authentic Ottoman craftsmanship from mass production.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) for a sensory feast of saffron, sumac, dried fruits, Turkish delight, and artisan honeys. Afterward, visit the magnificent Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably the finest work of Ottoman master architect Mimar Sinan — for its serene courtyard and sweeping Golden Horn views.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Turkish hammam experience at Çemberlitaş Hamamı or Çağaloğlu Hamamı — both 16th-century imperial bathhouses. Book the private VIP suite for an exclusive kese (exfoliation) and foam massage experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Pandeli Restaurant, above the Spice Bazaar entrance — a beloved Istanbul institution since 1901, serving classic Ottoman-Turkish dishes in a stunning tiled dining room
meals.dinner: Neolokal Restaurant, SALT Galata — Chef Maksut Aşkar's avant-garde take on Anatolian culinary heritage in a beautifully restored Ottoman bank building

day_by_day.notes: Hire a reputable guide for the Grand Bazaar to avoid being steered toward commission-based shops. Hammam reservations for private suites should be made several days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private cultural deep-dive into the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, arguably surpassing even those in Hagia Sophia. A specialist art historian guide is highly recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — Istanbul's most atmospheric and photogenic historic districts. Wander colorful Ottoman-era Greek and Jewish quarters, visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople, browse antique shops, and photograph the iconic rainbow-painted houses of Balat.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking the Golden Horn, then dinner in the Fatih district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Forno Balat — an artisan café and bakery in the heart of Balat beloved for its sourdough, Turkish pastries, and local mezze plates. Casual but exceptional quality.
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant, near Chora Church — the only restaurant in the world that recreates authentic recipes from Ottoman palace banquet records dating to the 15th and 16th centuries

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may have restricted access if restoration work is ongoing — verify current status before visiting. Balat streets are cobblestoned; wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a short ferry ride from the city. Arrive on Büyükada, the largest island, where no motorized vehicles are permitted. Hire a horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) or bicycle to tour the island's Victorian-era wooden mansions, pine forests, and hilltop Greek Orthodox monastery of Saint George.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the quieter lanes of Büyükada, swim at a designated beach area, or simply relax at a waterfront café watching the sea traffic. Visit a local artisan workshop or browse the small boutiques near the ferry dock.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul as the sun sets over the Marmara Sea — a genuinely magical experience. Private transfer back to the resort for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Miltos Restaurant, Büyükada — a charming island institution serving fresh Marmara seafood and Greek-influenced mezes on a terrace overlooking the harbor
meals.dinner: In-resort dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy the beachfront setting and a curated Turkish-Mediterranean tasting menu with local wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Take the IDO or Şehir Hatları ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı — journey is approximately 60–90 minutes. The islands are popular on weekends; consider visiting mid-week if possible. Bring sunscreen and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Dolmabahçe Palace on the European Bosphorus shore — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman imperial residence that replaced Topkapi as the administrative center of the empire. Marvel at the 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier, gilded ceilings, and 285 rooms of European Baroque opulence fused with Ottoman aesthetics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beşiktaş and Nişantaşı neighborhoods — Istanbul's most upscale districts. Browse luxury Turkish fashion designers, contemporary art galleries, and the beautifully curated Istanbul Museum of Modern Art (Istanbul Modern) in its stunning new Renzo Piano-designed building in Karaköy.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails at a sophisticated rooftop lounge in Nişantaşı or Karaköy, followed by dinner at one of Istanbul's celebrated contemporary restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Sunset Grill & Bar, Ulus — perched on a hillside with spectacular Bosphorus panoramas, serving premium Turkish and international cuisine
meals.dinner: Turk Fatih Tutak (TURK Restaurant) — a Michelin-starred experience from one of Turkey's most celebrated chefs, offering a modern tasting menu rooted in Anatolian ingredients and techniques

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays — verify schedule. Photography is restricted inside the palace. Book TURK Restaurant weeks in advance — it is Istanbul's most sought-after fine dining reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day cooking class with a professional Turkish chef — learn to prepare a full Ottoman-inspired menu including börek (savory pastries), imam bayıldı (stuffed eggplant), slow-braised lamb with dried fruits, and classic baklava. Classes typically held in a private kitchen studio in Beyoğlu or Cihangir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the bohemian Cihangir neighborhood — a favorite of Istanbul's artists, writers, and intellectuals. Browse independent bookshops, vintage stores, and contemporary art studios. Visit the Pera Museum for its outstanding collection of Orientalist paintings and the iconic 'Tortoise Trainer' by Osman Hamdi Bey.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical Ottoman music performance or a Whirling Dervish (Sema) ceremony — an authentic Sufi spiritual ritual of extraordinary beauty. Several venues in Sultanahmet and Beyoğlu host regular performances.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the morning cooking class — enjoy the fruits of your labor with your chef and fellow participants, paired with Turkish wines
meals.dinner: Ulus 29 — a legendary Istanbul venue combining a chic restaurant, bar, and terrace with unrivaled Bosphorus views and refined Turkish cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 5 days in advance. For the Whirling Dervish ceremony, the Hodjapasha Cultural Center in Sirkeci offers high-quality authentic performances most evenings — reserve tickets online.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Edirne — the former Ottoman capital located approximately 2.5 hours from Istanbul by private car. Begin with the Selimiye Mosque, considered Mimar Sinan's masterpiece and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, which Sinan himself declared his greatest achievement surpassing even the Hagia Sophia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Edirne's historic core — visit the Eski Cami (Old Mosque) with its enormous calligraphy, the beautifully restored Rüstem Pasha Caravanserai, and the Macedonian Tower. Browse the covered bazaar for Edirne's famous ciğer (liver) and local pastries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private car. Light dinner and relaxation at the resort after a full day of travel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lalezar Restaurant, Edirne — a well-regarded local institution famous for Edirne's signature tava ciğeri (pan-fried liver) and regional specialties
meals.dinner: Light dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — a selection of Turkish cold mezes, grilled fish, and fresh salads paired with a glass of local Thracian wine

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 08:00 to maximize time in Edirne. Hire a local guide in Edirne for deeper historical context. The drive passes through the beautiful Thrace countryside — enjoy the scenery en route.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Asian side of Istanbul — cross the Bosphorus by private boat or ferry to Üsküdar. Visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, stroll the atmospheric waterfront, and explore the historic Çamlıca Hill for the best panoramic views of the entire city, the Bosphorus, and the Marmara Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kadıköy — Istanbul's most vibrant and authentic neighborhood on the Asian shore. Visit the Kadıköy Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı) for artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh produce, and local delicacies. Browse the independent record stores, bookshops, and street art of Moda district.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset return boat crossing to the European side with views of the Istanbul skyline. Farewell-style dinner at a world-class restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Çiya Sofrası, Kadıköy — one of the most important restaurants in Turkey, run by culinary anthropologist Chef Musa Dağdeviren, preserving rare and forgotten Anatolian recipes from across the country
meals.dinner: Nicole Restaurant, Tomtom Suites — a rooftop fine dining gem offering contemporary Turkish cuisine with an exceptional natural wine program and sweeping Golden Horn views

day_by_day.notes: Çiya Sofrası is a must-visit for serious food lovers — the menu changes daily based on seasonal and regional ingredients. Arrive early as it fills up quickly even for lunch. Book Nicole in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Topkapi Palace Museum's special collections — focus on the Imperial Treasury, the miniature paintings collection, and the clocks and watches collection. Follow with a walk through the historic Gülhane Park adjacent to the palace walls, one of Istanbul's oldest public parks with rose gardens and Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury farewell spa day at the resort or at one of Istanbul's premier luxury hotel spas (such as the Four Seasons Bosphorus or Çırağan Palace Kempinski). Indulge in an Ottoman ritual bath, aromatherapy massage, and full body treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon of leisure — return to a favorite neighborhood, complete any last-minute luxury shopping at Nişantaşı or the Grand Bazaar, or simply relax at the resort's beachfront with a book and a glass of Turkish wine.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate final Turkish breakfast spread at the resort — make it a celebration
meals.lunch: Balıkçı Sabahattin, Sultanahmet — Istanbul's most beloved traditional fish restaurant, serving impeccably fresh Bosphorus and Marmara seafood in a charming historic setting
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Çırağan Palace Kempinski's Tuğra Restaurant — the pinnacle of Istanbul fine dining, set within a 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus, serving classical Ottoman court cuisine with extraordinary elegance

day_by_day.notes: Book Tuğra Restaurant at Çırağan Palace well in advance — request a window table overlooking the Bosphorus for the ultimate farewell experience. This is the perfect final dinner in Istanbul.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort and take a last walk along the beachfront. Soak in the views, reflect on 13 extraordinary days, and make any final purchases of Turkish souvenirs — artisan olive oil, saffron, hand-painted ceramics, or a box of premium Turkish delight from Hacı Bekir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport for departure. Arrive at the airport with ample time to explore the world-class duty-free shopping and dining options at Istanbul Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast at the resort — savor every last bite
meals.lunch: IGA Istanbul Airport — dine at one of the premium airport restaurants such as Simit Sarayı Premium or a sit-down Turkish restaurant in the international departures terminal
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Istanbul Airport check-in and security. The airport is vast — factor in walking time between terminals. Consider purchasing vacuum-packed Turkish cheeses, wines, or specialty foods from the airport's premium food market as final gifts.
